prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System: Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell; airports: Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport; local/statutory authority retained. Aliases: Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron; Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin; Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone; Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard; Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove; Tower Supervisor=Brindle(section-only voice drills); Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline(voice/chat). Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange: Flight Intent Message(route/timing/registration/turnaround/crew/connections); Identity Access Service authenticates; Business Rules Registry maps carriers; invalid/incomplete rejected(machine-readable reasons); material intents supersede schedules; changes require messages. Saffron maintains intents/readiness/constraints; checks legality/rotations/maintenance/passengers. Marlinstone predicts demand; Capacity Assessment Module compares Airport Capacity Plan/Airport Acceptance Rate; Storm Cell Snapshot qualifies confidence. Slot Allocation Engine→Adapter/Portal: Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time. Ground Delay Program: Slot Coordinator checks equity/feasibility,logs adjustments/conflicts; Copperfin authorizes baseline/recovery/divergence. Orchard validates identity/time/location/units; retains probability/provenance/version/override; degradation visible; low-confidence capacity provisional; shall issue timestamped coordination updates. Meteorology Briefing Officer interprets confidence/impact-timing; override preserves authoritative source. Time Synchronization Service→Audit Event Ledger: timestamps; shall align tower/duty-desk/surveillance/portal times. Alert Distribution Hub→Copperfin/Tower Supervisor/Saffron/accountable updater; distributes approved runway/taxi/apron-change alerts. Capacities→North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Ramp Movement Board(weather/taxi correlation)→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Portal(consolidated advisory positions/movements unless controller/authority confirms). Tower Sequence Manager uses validated status; controller judgment/radio procedures remain. Tower Supervisor/Airport Duty Manager resolve observation/surveillance conflicts before dissemination; duty desk confirms status; Runway Inspection Note precedes capacity endorsement. Supervisor verifies runway reductions against traffic/workload/safety; Manager verifies checks before rate/metering-change requests; authorized confirmations logged. Confirmed local position→Platform→Capacity Assessment Module recalculation,never local safety judgment. Portal

New part:
S205: East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor indications are used as supporting evidence, but the Ramp Control Lead remains responsible for reconciling sensor data with visual and operational reports.
S206: The Ramp Control Lead assigns priority to towing movements that remove a blocking aircraft, protect a confirmed departure sequence, or create capacity for an inbound aircraft with no equivalent stand option.
S207: Routine maintenance tows are normally sequenced behind live departure and arrival movements unless an operational safety issue requires earlier action.
S208: Ramp Control Lead sends the Stand Tow Request Form when a parked aircraft must be repositioned to release a stand, remove an apron blockage, or support a confirmed operating plan.
S209: Apron occupancy is managed as a time-based resource, with each stand treated as unavailable from the start of servicing until the aircraft and equipment are clear of the marked safety area.
S210: The Gate Conflict Detector alerts the Ramp Control Lead when a planned arrival, departure, or tow would create an overlapping occupancy condition at a stand or adjacent service lane.
S211: When a conflict is detected, the Ramp Control Lead coordinates with the Ground Handling Dispatcher to confirm whether servicing progress, equipment availability, or staffing constraints can change the sequence.
S212: The Handling Resource Planner provides the shared planning basis for baggage, catering, cleaning, boarding support, and towing resources that affect apron readiness.
S213: The Ramp Control Lead reviews Handling Resource Planner constraints before committing to a pushback sequence that depends on rapid equipment removal or immediate stand reuse.
S214: Airline Operations Coordinator participation is required when a resequence would materially affect passenger boarding, connection protection, or aircraft rotation plans.
S215: The Aircraft Operator Representative remains accountable for operator acceptance of any revised off-block expectation that results from ramp resequencing.
S216: Marlinstone shall refresh stand demand forecasts when the Ramp Movement Board records a material change in planned off-block timing.
S217: The Tower Sequence Manager receives the current ramp intent through system synchronization so that apron releases and runway metering remain consistent.
S218: If apron congestion begins to affect runway delivery, the Ramp Control Lead escalates the condition to the Tower Supervisor and Airport Duty Manager for a coordinated mitigation decision.
S219: During Adverse Weather Mode, the Ramp Control Lead increases spacing between pushbacks and towing movements to account for slower ground servicing and reduced driver visibility.
S220: During Capacity Reduction State, apron movements are prioritized to prevent stand saturation and to preserve access for emergency routes and critical service lanes.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
